question.text: A put option on USDINR with strike Rs 84.00 has a premium of Rs 0.50 when USDINR spot is Rs 83.50. What is its intrinsic value?

answer.text: Rs 0.50 (K - S = 84.00 - 83.50 = 0.50, and the premium is also 0.50, so time value is zero)
Rs 0 (the put is out of the money)

explanation.text: The Logic: For an in-the-money put, intrinsic value is X - S with a minimum of zero, so 84.00 - 83.50 = Rs 0.50. Time value is premium minus intrinsic value, so 0.50 - 0.50 = Rs 0. The Trap: This put is in the money because the strike exceeds the spot. The intrinsic value is the difference between strike and spot, not the spot or strike alone. Note: The same put intrinsic formula max(X - S, 0) applies generally to put options.
